messages.content: We can sign A or B and we get one security review this quarter. A is 40 a seat, data stays in our VPC, onboarding is a month. B is 85 a seat, they host, and it can be on by Friday. There are 12 seats. Walk both paths, try to kill your pick, and say what a one-day mistake would cost.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=extreme|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Path A. Twelve seats at 40 is 480 a month, plus a month before anyone uses it, and the data stays in the VPC so the review slot is not spent on a new host. Path B. Twelve seats at 85 is 1020 a month, 540 more than A, and Friday is real, and the review slot is consumed by their hosting. Over a year the price gap is 540 × 12 = 6480, which is real money and still smaller than a blocked quarter if the slot was the only way to ship something else. The binding constraint in the note is the slot, not the 540. First pick is A. Kill attempt: onboarding slips past the quarter. Then A bought nothing this quarter and B's Friday would have. That is a risk to write down, not a fact, so it becomes a flip condition. Kill attempt: the 12 people are idle without the tool and a week of their time exceeds 540. Possible, and not in the note. I will not invent their burn rate. Kill attempt: a standing review already covers B. Also absent. A one-day mistake, meaning we sign the wrong one and reverse tomorrow, costs the contract's cooling-off if there is one, which nobody stated, so I won't pretend it's free. The pick that survives the stated facts is A, with two written flip conditions and no invented salary math.
</think>

Sign A. Twelve seats makes B 540 a month more, and B also spends the only review. Flip if A's month slips past the quarter, or if B's host is already covered by a standing review. I won't price a one-day reversal, because no cooling-off term is in what you wrote.
